_doc: v79.12.7 (item 7): the text residue's tables (src/rag/text_hygiene.py). Patterns are Python regexes, case-insensitive. stance_words / stance_prefixes: a parenthesis holding only a ruling's stance on an element («(contro)», «(a favore)», «(verso l'integrazione: contro)») -- the registry's and the thesis call's wording -- is dropped from every text outside the tables and the quoted passages, as an element code is. internal_notes: the wording of a list's draft status (79.12.5 item 8: the 168-bis list's status lives in data/lawyer_method.json «status», never printed) -- a sentence holding one is removed and counted. procedural_acts: a procedural act narrated (the PM's contestazione, an avviso, a notifica, the rinvio a giudizio, a decreto) is a certain fact: the act's sentence is «accertato» unless what is left of it once the act's own words are taken out is attributed or hedged; procedural_act_modals (review): a sentence holding a modal or a conditional («il PM potrebbe contestare», «la notifica sarebbe avvenuta») narrates no act done -- it is read as any other sentence; procedural_act_hedges_ignored are the hedge words that describe the act's own content («ipotizzando che …»). An act's sentence grounds «provato» (or «non risulta») only for an element naming the act (its «stems»): it proves that the act was done, not what it charges. cenni_rule_verbs: the verbs that, beside rule_statements.RULE_VERBS, make a sentence of a «Cenni» section a rule statement; cenni_min_shared / cenni_min_share: the content words such a sentence must share with one comma of the article it cites (or, naming none, of the articles its section cites, else of the cenni's articles) -- at least min_shared words and at least min_share of its own -- unless it traces to an element of that article's record; cenni_absolutes (review): a sentence sharing those words is still not grounded when it inverts the comma (a word the comma negates it asserts, or the reverse) or adds an absolute the comma does not hold («sempre», «in ogni caso» …). code_context_patterns (review): with no record's code known (a text the method did not write), a sentence holding a bare R-code and one of these words uses it as an element («contesta R2», «l'elemento R2») and is removed, as an R-code is never the reader's. headless_dates: the forms of a date the citation check removes with a headless reference, and finds orphaned before a closing parenthesis.
